newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere up on highly increased turnover.
newsitem.headline: Solidere up on highly increased turnover.

text.p: Solidere shares rose on higher turnover on Thursday, and dealers linked increased demand to news that the company began marketing Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) worth $115-$125 million for issue on November 26.
A shares rose to $115 from Wednesday's $114 on the Beirut Stock Exchange and B shares also rose slightly to $118 from $117.625.
"There was big demand on a higher price in the second fixing, obviously it is the positive reaction to the GDR issue," a dealer said.
Another dealer said only one bloc of 10,000 demand orders for A shares set on $115 pushed the price up.
"The rise resulted from this intervention which is definitely linked to the GDR issue," he added.
Turnover in Solidere shares more than doubled to 14,098 shares from Wednesday's 6,167 and value was $1,629,459.375 from $710,811.75.
Market sources said on Tuesday that each GDR would be worth one tenth of one of Solidere's shares. The price range on the GDRs was $11.5 to $12.5 for an issue price of $115-$125 million.
A Solidere executive questioned by Reuters on the report declined to comment.
There was no trade in the four other companies listed on the BSE: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index rose 0.17 percent to 84.72 and the BLOM stock index also rose 0.46 percent to 988.95.
